_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. status: active = connector-only, a reprint would clobber it; upstreamed = also fixed in the press, a reprint from a fixed press regenerates it, but the back-port must still be present today.

handfixes.summary: Better Stack updates are PATCH; monitors/heartbeats update + MCP update path call PatchWithParams, not PutWithParams
handfixes.why: Better Stack's Update endpoints are HTTP PATCH (partial update); a PUT 405s. Prior prints hand-fixed PUT->PATCH post-generate. The durable home is the spec (`method: PATCH`, which 4.22 emits natively as PatchWithParams), but the back-port must be present in the generated client + update commands today or every update fails.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Encode `method: PATCH` on the update operations in the press spec so PatchWithParams is emitted by construction (4.22+ supports this).

handfixes.summary: Live fan-out parsers decode IDs with json.Number + dec.UseNumber() so 7+ digit monitor IDs don't render in scientific notation
handfixes.why: Better Stack monitor/resource IDs are 7+ digits. An `any`->float64->%v decode renders them as 1.234e+06, silently breaking mirror joins (false 'monitor missing' + suppressed real drift). Only round-2 adversarial review caught it; the unit test masked it with a 5-digit ID. json.Number preserves the exact integer. Lives in the hand-authored statuspage-audit novel and the store decode path.

handfixes.summary: gen_governance keyword classifier mis-tiered incident verbs; hand-corrected: acknowledge/resolve/import -> Write, triage/workflow-archive -> Read
handfixes.why: gen_governance.py keyword-matches command paths and ignores pp:method, so for this incident/monitoring connector it BOTH false-negatived real writes (`incidents acknowledge`, `incidents resolve`, verb-less `import`) into Read AND false-positived read-only `triage` (a local incident board view) and `workflow archive` (local-only sync) into Write. The tiers were hand-corrected against the real method surface (12 routine writes). A full reprint re-runs gen_governance and would re-introduce the mis-tiering. See project_betterstack_onboard_gotchas, project_gen_governance_misses_verbless_writes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make gen_governance method-aware off agent-context pp:method (fleet-wide fix); until then this hand-correction recurs on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For betterstack the manifest gained: BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL. server.json gained: BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name, and no file stores operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds; applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Each operator-named write (profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl and the learn tables: learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns) goes through the credential kit's file or SQL sink, which withholds one that carries a credential the program holds. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>. The connector's own RefuseHeld checks on each journal, log, profile, feedback, learning, playbook, candidate, lookup and pattern write are replaced by the kit's sinks (credkit-wiring, credkit-sqlite-every-handle), so every line that does reach a file passes the kit's matcher as one unit.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: raw Betterstack bodies never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Work order: nothing but the credential store holds a credential. c.NoCache = true in guardClient (betterstack_guard.go); TestGuardWrapsTheTransport asserts it. README and SKILL say responses are never cached.

handfixes.summary: Every resource write passes withoutStoredSecrets (internal/store/stored_secret_fields.go), which masks every credential-named value by the one secret-name rule (cliutil.RedactSecretFields), so a monitor is kept with its auth_username, auth_password and request_headers masked and an escalation policy with its incident_token masked. Every SQL statement then passes the kit's SQL driver (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Work order: no credential in files. The kit's SQL driver withholds a whole statement that carries a held value, and a monitor's credential pair and request headers and a policy's incident_token are held response fields, so without the mask a sync of monitors or policies would store nothing. TestMonitorCredentialsNeverPrint checks the record is stored, masked. The old storedID rewrite and withhold driver are retired with the old layer.

handfixes.summary: No MCP tool changes Betterstack state: every endpoint tool is a GET marked read-only and every mirrored command is read-only or writes only the CLI's own files. The confirm gate stays installed so a mirrored command a later print adds that is neither read-only nor local previews and sends only with confirm: true.
handfixes.why: Work order: an MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/betterstack_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools after RegisterAll. TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm fails on any registered tool that is not read-only, not on its local list and has no confirm gate; TestMCPSendsOnlyReads (black-box) checks a full MCP battery sends only GETs and the two logins.

handfixes.why: The generated docs describe the press defaults (a response cache) that the credential layer turns off; a reprint restores the false promise and drops the transcripts reasoning the work order requires.

handfixes.summary: A client built under --dry-run refuses every request at its transport, so no write can reach Better Stack whatever a command does with the client.
handfixes.why: Defense in depth: the generated preview path returns before sending, and this transport makes a missed branch fail closed. The black-box test runs writes under --dry-run from a cold start against a fake API host and counts zero requests.

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (every create, update and delete tool, incidents_acknowledge, incidents_resolve) returns a preview of the request and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true; the gate wraps every non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so one a later print adds is gated too. A preview shows a credential-named argument (a monitor's auth_password or request_headers) as [redacted] (previewArguments, cliutil.RedactSecretFields), so the kit does not withhold the whole preview.
handfixes.why: Work order connector note: every MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. Press 4.34.2's in-process endpoint handlers (makeAPIHandler) send writes directly. The gate (hand file internal/mcp/betterstack_endpoint_confirm.go) is installed by one anchored line in the generated tools.go after every registration and before the read-only drop. The black-box test drives the real MCP server against a fake Better Stack: no write without confirm, the string "true" previews, and boolean true sends (control).

handfixes.summary: A config rewrite adds no credential to config.toml: config.toml keeps its own base_url, never BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL's (configForSave), so a userinfo password or query credential in BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL never lands in the file; a saved token goes to the 0600 credential store. config.toml and the store are credential SOURCES (orchestrator ruling 7): written outside the kit through cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, named in Declarations.Files and held whole on every read and write.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 class credential-persisted-outside-the-store: `BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL='https://uptime.betterstack.com/api/v2?api_key=X' auth set-token` wrote X (and a userinfo password) into config.toml, because the generated save persists base_url as configured. The old persistence filter (betterstack_persist.go) is retired with the old layer; the source-side fix is that a rewrite keeps the file's own values. TestP1ConfigRewriteAddsNoCopyOfTheURLPassword covers the environment password beside a [headers] value; TestConfigFileNeverHoldsACredential (black box) the query credential.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file (written through the kit's credkit.NewWriter) on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. Under the retired output filter the unclosed file was a pipe that kept the process from exiting (`export monitors --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung; TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError); the kit's writer is closed on the same path.

handfixes.summary: The Authorization bearer token and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the configured base URL (https://uptime.betterstack.com/api/v2, or BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL); every redirect hop must stay on that origin, a non-ASCII host never matches, and an unparseable base URL pins nothing (every request refused). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/betterstack_guard.go), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the Authorization header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the named auth headers, so a Location to another host or an absolute path from an MCP argument would carry the token off the vendor API. One origin, taken from the configured base URL; an operator who sets BETTERSTACK_BASE_URL moves the pin with it. The pin runs before the kit's transport (client.OutboundGuard), which holds every credential a response carries; the pin itself holds nothing.

handfixes.why: press-traps s5: the fleet doctor replay restored doctor_verdict.go with doctorShippedBaseURL = "https://uptime.betterstack.com/api/v2", so doctor printed "not configured (base_url is a placeholder)" and skipped the credential probe on every correctly configured install. handfixes.summary: The credential-name rule and the kit's declarations are pinned against Better Stack's own spec in both directions: of every spec name exactly the Authorization carrier and an escalation policy's incident_token read as credentials, and the declared ResponseFields, CredentialFields and MCPArguments are incident_token plus the monitor credentials the API documents outside spec.yaml (auth_username, auth_password, request_headers, in every separator spelling), none of which is a spec name. The names live in internal/cliutil/testdata/betterstack-spec-names.json (the published module ships no spec) and are checked against spec.yaml when it sits beside the module
handfixes.why: press-traps s2 (salesbuildr -> backup-radar): a spec-name guard that read spec.json silently skipped on this spec.yaml connector. Pinned names cannot skip.

Tests seen failing first (seen/incomplete-snapshot-seen-failing.log). The sync wrapper records filtered walks by parameter NAME only (betterstack_sync_scope.go). (betterstack 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: A monitor's request_headers (name and value pairs whose values carry the probed site's own credentials, an Authorization or X-Api-Key header among them) is a declared credential container: the kit holds every value beneath it in a response, a request body and an MCP argument, and the store and an MCP preview mask the whole list (credentialContainerNames). A header under a name that is no credential's (X-Tenant) is held too: the kit reads no sibling member.
handfixes.why: Class credential-named-by-sibling-member, found by the black box on Better Stack's documented monitor request_headers shape: the value sat under `value`, a name no rule reads as a credential, and printed in every output mode and over MCP and landed in the store, export.jsonl, deliver.json and learnings.jsonl. The old layer's pair rule is retired with it; the declaration over-holds the container's non-credential values (a P2 cost, .review/followups.md).

handfixes.summary: export (CLI and the MCP export tool) walks every page: each resourceReadConfigs entry pages with page / per_page instead of declaring no pagination
handfixes.why: Wrong result on Better Stack's documented paging (page / per_page lists, pagination.next): the 4.34.2 render gave every read config no pagination, so export wrote the first page only (50 of 130 records in the black box), silently, exit 0, to a file documented as a backup. sync pages correctly (its own pager). tools/apply_edits.py re-applies the edit on every render; the durable home is a `pagination:` block (type page, cursor_param page, limit_param per_page) on each list endpoint in spec.yaml. Seen failing: seen/export-first-page-only-seen-failing.log, seen/export-first-page-only-seen-failing-main.log. (betterstack 4.34.2 reprint)
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Add `pagination: {type: page, cursor_param: page, limit_param: per_page}` to each list endpoint in spec.yaml so resource_paths.go renders paged read configs by construction.

handfixes.summary: A monitor's basic-auth username is a credential: auth_username is a declared CredentialField, ResponseField and MCPArgument in every separator spelling (auth_username, authUsername, auth_user, authUser; the kit compares names ignoring case, so AUTHUSER and authuser are authUser), so the kit holds it before any sink; the one secret-name rule (credentialIdentityName) reads the same names so the store and an MCP preview mask it. Names that only mention users (on_call_users, user_id, last_login_at) stay visible.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] holder incomplete: Better Stack's documented monitor auth_username (beside auth_password) matched no credential rule, so `monitors get --data-source live --json` printed it. Print-review P1 input (open after the r1 fix): the same value under AUTHUSER. TestP1PairIdentityInAnyCaseNeverPrints runs that input on the built binary against a TLS fake and was seen failing on the pre-kit build.

handfixes.summary: Every config file any --config on the command line names is held inside credkit.Start, before any output (credentialFiles: holdOnly(runFiles(cfg)) for each), so a config the parser never reached cannot print in an unknown-command or flag error.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] alternate-config credentials unheld: the startup holder loaded only BETTERSTACK_CONFIG or the default path, so `betterstack-cli <token> --config alt.toml` printed alt.toml's api_token in its unknown-command error. MCP cannot reach the read (betterstack-mcp has no --config and refuses one). The old startup holder is retired with the old layer; TestBsR1CommandLineConfigIsHeldBeforeParse (black box) and TestMalformedConfigNeverPrintsAtStartup run on the built binaries.

handfixes.summary: Every plain sync is a full walk (no incremental from= window on GET /incidents), and a walk that sends --since, --latest-only or --full=false is recorded as not a snapshot, so the novels refuse it instead of reading a time window as the whole account. Every walk (sync, auto-refresh, workflow archive) passes one door, syncResource in betterstack_sync_scope.go, and auto-refresh is itself a whole walk
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] filtered incident snapshot read as complete (a new instance of the pre-closed class incomplete-snapshot-read-as-complete): `sync --since 7d` sent from=<date> (spec.yaml resources.incidents.endpoints.list.params[from]) and every later plain sync sent from=<last sync>, so an incident open since before the window was never stored and one stored open was never seen resolved; triage reported both wrong. The scope record is an allowlist (only a full, reconciling, unparameterized walk is a snapshot). Codex review round 1 (betterstack 4.34.2 reprint); test seen failing first on the round-1 code: seen/r1-time-filtered-walk-read-as-complete-seen-failing.log. Codex round 2 reopened the class: auto-refresh (and workflow archive) called the generated walk directly, around the record on the sync command, so a refresh with from=<last sync> saved a complete checkpoint and triage kept a resolved incident open. The generated walk is renamed syncResourceWalk so no caller can go around the door, and a re-render that restores the old name fails the build. Auto-refresh walks the whole resource: recording its old one-page walk as partial would have made every novel refuse once an hour. TestAutoRefreshNeverKeepsAResolvedIncidentOpen and TestEveryWalkShapeIsRecordedWhereTheWalkRuns were seen failing first.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit, and every early exit of the MCP main returns through it; the API client (client.OutboundGuard, under the origin pin), feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit (response and platform cache, export, deliver, feedback, journal, teach logs, run profiles, client profiles, the legacy-store claim marker, the rate-limit stamp); the MCP stdio and HTTP servers pass credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP and MCPTools; the MCP mirror runs the CLI with credkit.RunCommand; stdout is asked about through credkit.Terminal. The store and config rewrites go outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile) as declared credential sources. A config or credential file is held with credkit.HoldBody and credkit.HoldURL every time it is read, a token read from a pipe is held as stdin, a dry-run preview's body is held (cliutil.HoldBody) before it prints, a built auth header and a resolved client-profile value are held where they enter, and the MCP server's --tls-key file is held at startup. A run profile treats a flag the one secret-name rule names as a credential flag.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. It closes the three open print-review P1 inputs (a monitor's basic-auth user under AUTHUSER, a 2-character password inside a hex-escaped name, a password inside a headerless deflate stream nested in a member) and the open review classes: a malformed config's credential in a startup flag error, doctor's credentials verdict (no name-based redaction), the env-schema gate (no EnvOverride holder over every variable), and the MCP HTTP no-token refusal printed before os.Exit (credkit.Exit drains it). Tests: internal/credwire/leak_test.go, on the built binaries, seen failing on the pre-kit HEAD or with credkit.Start removed. Retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, secure-container-is-credential, r1-holder-reads-every-part, r1-mixed-byte-escapes-decoded, r1-split-across-deliveries-withheld, held-value-case-folded, output-units-reassembled, preclose-holder-numbers-and-cookies, preclose-escape-fixpoint, preclose-split-across-processes-and-protocol, refuse-held-uses-connector-chokepoint, output-derived-and-scheme-forms-matched-whole, g304-paths-cleaned-not-annotated, r1-short-value-encodings-withheld, r1-file-history-is-the-whole-file, r2-short-value-nested-encodings, r1-credential-split-across-deliveries, r1-decoder-bound-read-as-no-echo, r1-persistence-gate-narrower-than-chokepoint, startup-error-lost, r1-short-held-value-inside-other-text and r1-secret-in-headerless-compressed-stream: replaced by the shared credential kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json backs). Retires r1-unreadable-history-read-as-empty and r1-check-then-append-not-serialized too: a credential split across two runs of the program is contract section 6 item 5 (advisory), and the history check and file lock (betterstack_filelock.go) that served them are gone; the kit reconciles a file's history on open. The kit holds every contract section 1 source at startup and on arrival and withholds at every sink as one stream, so the connector's own holder, decoded funnel, output chokepoint, file and network writers, SQL withhold driver, argv refusal and exit shim are gone, with their tests.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring and the Declarations literal.

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter credsql applies as each connection opens. The read-only opener runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included. The kit checks each statement once against its matcher, so the internal/store suite no longer pays the old per-statement decode of the retired withhold driver.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name, and express the MCP sql value cap as a connection-open setting.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: --stdin is a declared StdinFlag, so the kit holds a body whole and line by line before anything prints. cliutil.CompactStdinBody puts a JSON body on one line first, because a line of { alone collides with public text and refuses the start. feedback --stdin refuses instead of reporting a record the kit would withhold.
handfixes.why: A monitor body (monitors create or update --stdin) carries auth_password and request_headers, and a held body is the kit's to judge. The cost: a --dry-run preview of a --stdin body, and a vendor answer repeating part of it, are withheld whole, and the write still happens.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate StdinFlags and the compaction with the kit wiring.

handfixes.summary: credentialFiles returns the config the program really uses first, because the kit takes the base URL and every allowed origin from the first file naming one: an explicit --config or BETTERSTACK_CONFIG wins, the last --home decides the default paths, and every other file any flag could mean is only held. The credential stores and run profile stores are only held too: config.Load takes no base URL from a store. Startup reads --config and --home by every occurrence; the root pre-run refuses a run whose parsed values differ (another flag swallowed one), so a file the run does not use never names the allowed origin. betterstack-mcp, which has no such flags, refuses to start when startup read one.
handfixes.why: A discovered default's or a store's base_url must not become an allowed origin for a credential from another file.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the file discovery in the wiring file.

handfixes.summary: Every report's readCommandResources entry (auto_refresh.go) names every resource its loaders read, so automatic refresh renews each one past the freshness window; statuspage-audit now refreshes heartbeats, which it reads for a page's heartbeat entries
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] class stale-dependent-resource (betterstack 0.1.8, credential kit branch): statuspage-audit's entry listed status-pages, monitors and incidents, but its loaders also read heartbeats, and requireFinishedSync accepts any finished sync however old. A heartbeat paused in Better Stack after the last sync stayed unpaused in the store, and `statuspage-audit --json` returned no findings with live_check ok. The press generates readCommandResources from spec.Cache.Commands, and no spec ships in this repo, so the entry is a hand edit to a generated file. TestStatuspageAuditRefreshesTheHeartbeatsItReads was seen failing first on the round-1 code. TestEveryReportRefreshesEveryResourceItReads is the class guard: it finds every command whose body reaches requireFinishedSync from the package source, runs each against a synced store with the requireFinishedSyncSeen hook (betterstack_snapshot.go), and fails when a report reads a resource its entry does not refresh or has no entry at all; seen failing on the old statuspage-audit list, on a removed heartbeat-risk entry and on group-health without monitor-groups.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
